Answer Part 2: Spec DD (5 pt)

Specification-Driven Development guarantees that implementation and testing are anchored in formal, unambiguous requirements. The system specification was committed at cf54f91 in docs/lab-04/specification.md before any code was written.

2.1 Core Functional Requirements & Business Rules Breakdown
Requirement RefSpecification DescriptionEnforcement & Verification Mechanism
AC-01..03, BR-01..03 IT Staff / Admin action logging; identity derivation performedById and createdById bound to authenticated JWT token; client spoofing ignored.
AC-04..07, BR-04..05 Field validations and follow-up requirements Duration > 0, description ≥ 10 chars, past/present date. followUpNote required if followUpRequired = true.
AC-08..10, FR-07 Requester read isolation Requesters can only view actions on tickets they created; accessing others returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
AC-14, BR-10 Append-only audit trail No DELETE route implemented; historical actions are permanently preserved.
AC-15..17, BR-13 Strict Resolution Gate Enforcement Blocks transition to RESOLVED unless ticket has owner, ≥1 action taken, ≥1 completed action with result, and addressed follow-ups.
AC-18..19, BR-14 Atomic Concurrency Control Database write predicates: updateMany({ where: { id, version } }) returning HTTP 409 Conflict.
Part 6, BR-19..23 Action Lifecycle & Assignee ActionStatus enum (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED), active assignee validation, terminal lock.
Part 7, BR-25..26 Append-only Status History TicketStatusHistory written in exact same transaction as ticket status changes.
2.2 Ticket & Action State Transition State Machines
Ticket Status Transitions (BR-12, BR-13)
  • NEW → OPEN, CANCELLED
  • OPEN → IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER, CANCELLED
  • IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED (Resolution Gate!), WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER, CANCELLED
  • WAITING_FOR_REQUESTER → IN_PROGRESS, CANCELLED
  • RESOLVED → CLOSED, REOPENED
  • CLOSED, CANCELLED → Terminal (Immutable)
Action Taken Lifecycle (Part 6, BR-19..24)
  • PENDING → IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED
  • IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED, CANCELLED
  • COMPLETED → Terminal (Mandatory result required)
  • CANCELLED → Terminal (Immutable)
  • Assigned to active IT Staff/Admin only (Requesters and inactive rejected with 400).
2.3 Definition of Done (DoD)

Features require 100% bidirectional traceability, Red-to-Green automated unit/integration tests, zero horizontal scrollbar across 360px/768px/1280px viewports, 0 Axe-core accessibility violations, and peer review sign-off.

4.3 Student Self-Reflection

What AI Did Exceptionally Well: Antigravity excelled at rapid spec translation, generating complete TypeScript types, and authoring rigorous edge-case tests. Formulating multi-threaded async tests (Promise.all) to prove atomic concurrency conflicts was remarkably fast and accurate.

Where Human Oversight Was Vital: Human judgment was essential in navigating the ambiguity between "append-only audit logs" and "operational lifecycle tasks," choosing a model where in-flight tasks can be updated but completed tasks are terminally locked. Human insight also drove the shift from in-memory version checking to database-level write predicates.

Key Takeaway: Spec-Driven and Test-Driven Development serve as essential guardrails when working with AI. By defining contracts and assertions first, the AI's speed is harnessed while eliminating hallucinations and regressions.

Answer Part 6: Working Actions Taken UI (10 pt)

The Actions Taken subsystem records real operational work, enforces an active assignee lifecycle, locks completed actions terminally, and protects concurrent writes via atomic database predicates.

Figure 6.1: Actions Taken Subsystem (Desktop 1440px) displaying Status Badges (Pending, In Progress, Completed), operational assignee delegation, quick transition buttons, and the (Terminal / Immutable) lock indicator.
Figure 6.2: Optimistic Concurrency 409 Conflict Alert. When two staff members edit simultaneously, the losing update is blocked and a red warning banner prompts to reload latest data without silent data loss.
Figure 6.3: Requester Read-Only View. Requesters can inspect operational progress and notes on their tickets, but all creation and edit controls are completely excluded from the UI and protected at the API layer.
6.1 Concurrency & Lifecycle Implementation Details
  • Active Operational Assignee: Any active IT Staff/Admin can be assigned (assigneeId). Assigning inactive staff or requesters is rejected with HTTP 400 (INACTIVE_ASSIGNEE).
  • Terminal Action Lock: Actions transitioned to COMPLETED or CANCELLED are permanently locked against further edits (HTTP 400 TERMINAL_ACTION_LOCKED).
  • Atomic Optimistic Concurrency: Updates use database write predicate updateMany({ where: { id, version: expectedVersion } }) inside a database transaction. If another user committed a change first, 0 rows update and the server returns HTTP 409 Conflict.
6.2 Atomic Concurrency Database Predicate Implementation (actions-taken.ts)
// Atomic compare-and-increment database predicate inside transaction (server/src/routes/actions-taken.ts)
const result = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
  const updateCount = await tx.actionTaken.updateMany({
    where: { id: actionId, ticketId, version: expectedVersion },
    data: { ...updateFields, version: expectedVersion + 1 }
  });
  if (updateCount.count === 0) {
    const latest = await tx.actionTaken.findUnique({ where: { id: actionId } });
    return { conflict: true, latest };
  }
  const updated = await tx.actionTaken.findUnique({ where: { id: actionId } });
  return { conflict: false, updated };
});
if (result.conflict) {
  return res.status(409).json({ error: 'Conflict Detected: Action was modified by another user.', current: result.latest });
}
Answer Part 7: Working Ticket Workflow (5 pt)

The Ticket Workflow subsystem enforces a strict state machine, protects status updates with atomic concurrency control, blocks premature resolution via the 4-condition Resolution Gate, and logs an append-only audit trail in TicketStatusHistory.

Figure 7.1: Strict Resolution Gate Rejection Banner on ticket TKT-2026-001233. Attempting to select RESOLVED without actions triggers an inline alert; status remains safely in OPEN.
Figure 7.2: Append-Only Ticket Status History Timeline rendering chronological transitions with from/to statuses, timestamps, and actor identity.
7.1 Resolution Gate Rules (BR-13) & Transactional History (BR-25, BR-26)
  1. Owner Assignment: Ticket must have an assigned owner (ownerId !== null).
  2. Recorded Actions: At least one Action Taken must exist under the ticket.
  3. Completed Action with Result: At least one Action Taken must be in COMPLETED status with non-empty result.
  4. Follow-up Notes Completed: All actions with followUpRequired = true must have completed followUpNote.
  5. Transactional Audit Trail: Every successful status transition writes exactly 1 row to TicketStatusHistory in the same database transaction. Concurrency conflicts roll back completely with 0 rows added.
7.2 Backend Resolution Gate Enforcement Code (staff.ts)
// Backend Resolution Gate verification before transition to RESOLVED (server/src/routes/staff.ts)
if (targetStatus === 'RESOLVED') {
  if (!ticket.ownerId) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Cannot resolve: Ticket must have an assigned owner.' });
  }
  const actions = await prisma.actionTaken.findMany({ where: { ticketId } });
  if (actions.length === 0) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Cannot resolve: Ticket has no Actions Taken recorded.' });
  }
  const completedWithResult = actions.some(a => a.status === 'COMPLETED' && a.result && a.result.trim().length > 0);
  if (!completedWithResult) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Cannot resolve: At least one completed Action Taken with documented result is required.' });
  }
  const pendingFollowups = actions.some(a => a.followUpRequired && (!a.followUpNote || a.followUpNote.trim().length === 0));
  if (pendingFollowups) {
    return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Cannot resolve: All required follow-up notes must be completed.' });
  }
}
